claims.text: The local release row and Bulbapedia raw source row place this CoroCoro Comic March 1999 issue insert on February 15, 1999.
The bounded source slice models two source-pinned identities: Blaine's Growlithe row 084 and Sabrina's Abra row 085.
Bulbapedia card-page release information describes each card as available on a two-card insert alongside the other in the March 1999 issue of CoroCoro Comic, released February 15, 1999.

The card pages expose an artist lineage involving Ken Sugimori and Atsuko Nishida across Gym print, Unnumbered Promotional print, and later Wizards/Nintendo Power memory. This dossier lists that lineage as route context and requires image/route checks instead of collapsing it into one unqualified print-authority claim.

This release matters because CoroCoro made two Gym Leader relationships collectible at once: Blaine and Growlithe as the warm fire-gym half, Sabrina and Abra as the psychic-gym half, both arriving before or beside later Gym expansion memory could swallow the route.

This source slice is not a complete CoroCoro issue archive, magazine-object ledger, copy-count authority, Gym-series promo census, image-rights grant, price source, condition source, or physical-card authentication source.

Agents should preserve the February 15 1999 CoroCoro March issue route, two-card insert relationship, row 084/085 identity, Japanese/romaji names when source-page supported, Gym-symbol promotional-addition context, and artist-lineage trap before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: CoroCoro March 1999 insert — Blaine and Sabrina before the Gym memory hardens
narrative.why_it_matters: This is CoroCoro doing one of its quiet little feats: taking two Gym Leader relationships and making them feel like something a reader received, not just something a set later organized. Blaine's Growlithe is warm, loyal, very human-scale fire. Sabrina's Abra is small, strange, and psychic in that early-Kanto way where a kid could feel the mystery before understanding the rules. The pair is not valuable because it is huge; it is valuable because the route is delicate. Name, Gym Leader, species, and artist memory all point toward other prints. The assembly is the magazine: February 15, 1999, March issue, two-card insert, rows 084 and 085.

narrative.human_title: Blaine's Growlithe — the warm half of the March 1999 insert
narrative.why_it_matters: Blaine's Growlithe is wonderful because it is modest. It is a companion card: small enough to feel like something a CoroCoro reader could tuck away, but bound to a strong character line through Blaine. The trap is that the broader Gym Heroes/Guren Town Gym memory is louder than the promo route. The agent should keep saying the quiet thing out loud: row 084, CoroCoro March 1999, two-card insert with Sabrina's Abra, exact image needed.

narrative.human_title: Sabrina's Abra — the psychic half of the March 1999 insert
narrative.why_it_matters: Sabrina's Abra has the exact collector problem this catalog is built for. The name pulls toward Gym Challenge. The English memory pulls toward Wizards Black Star. The character pulls toward Sabrina. But the object here is quieter and more specific: row 085, CoroCoro March 1999, a two-card insert with Blaine's Growlithe. It is a little psychic hinge in the magazine route, and the agent should protect that hinge from being smeared into every later Abra memory.
